title: Pushout products of free fixed-object simplicial-category cells
statement: Let $O$ be a small set, let $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ carry the fixed-object model structure of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] (local weak equivalences and local Kan fibrations), and for $u,v\in O$, the case $u=v$ allowed, let $F^O_{u,v}:\mathrm{sSet}\to\mathrm{sCat}_O$ be the free-arrow functor of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction]. For a small simplicial set $X$ and $C\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$ define $X\otimes C\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$ by letting $(X\otimes C)_n$ be the coproduct, among ordinary categories with object set $O$ and identity-on-objects functors, of copies $C_n^{(x)}$ of $C_n$ indexed by $x\in X_n$, a simplicial operator $\alpha$ sending the copy indexed by $x$ to the copy indexed by $\alpha^*x$ through $\alpha^*$; this is functorial in $X$ and $C$. Use simplicial sets, boundary and horn inclusions, monomorphisms and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ be a boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ ($m\geq0$) or a horn inclusion $\Lambda^m_k\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ ($m\geq1$), and let $j:P\hookrightarrow Q$ be any monomorphism of simplicial sets. Write $i\mathbin\square j:(Q\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times L)\to Q\times L$ and $$F^O_{u,v}(i)\mathbin\square j:(Q\otimes F^O_{u,v}(K))\amalg_{P\otimes F^O_{u,v}(K)}(P\otimes F^O_{u,v}(L))\longrightarrow Q\otimes F^O_{u,v}(L),$$ the pushout taken in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. Then there are isomorphisms $X\otimes F^O_{u,v}(Y)\cong F^O_{u,v}(X\times Y)$, natural in $X,Y$, under which $F^O_{u,v}(i)\mathbin\square j$ is identified with $F^O_{u,v}(i\mathbin\square j)$. This map is a cofibration of $\mathrm{sCat}_O$, and a trivial cofibration if $i$ is a horn inclusion or $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Section 7.1 and Proposition 7.2, pp.276-277; the free-cell tensor calculation is the degreewise free-generator calculation underlying the simplicial model axiom. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: In simplicial degree n, the category (X\otimes F^O_{u,v}(Y))_n is the coproduct over x\in X_n of a copy of the free category on the graph with one u\to v generator for each y\in Y_n. The coproduct of these copies is the free category on the disjoint union of those generators, namely the graph indexed by X_n\times Y_n. Faces and degeneracies send the generator labelled (x,y) to the one labelled (\alpha^*x,\alpha^*y), so these degreewise identifications assemble into a natural simplicial-category isomorphism X\otimes F^O_{u,v}(Y)\cong F^O_{u,v}(X\times Y). The construction also covers u=v, where arbitrary finite words in the loop generators are retained.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Section 7.1; degreewise free-generator calculation underlying the simplicial model axiom, pp.276--277. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the natural isomorphism of Step 1 to the four terms in the displayed pushout. Since the free-arrow functor is left adjoint to evaluation, its defining Hom bijection identifies the pushout of free arrows with the free arrow on the simplicial-set pushout: maps from either side into a fixed T are exactly compatible maps from the two input simplicial sets into T(u,v). Thus the pushout in sCat_O is naturally F^O_{u,v}((Q\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times L)), and the induced map is identified with F^O_{u,v}(i\mathbin\square j). Naturality in X,Y follows from the same universal-property calculation.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Section 7.1 and Proposition 7.2, pp.276--277; free-cell tensor and pushout comparison. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The simplicial-set helper [lem-coef-kan-quillen-cartesian-pushout-product] gives that r=i\mathbin\square j is a monomorphism, and that r is a weak homotopy equivalence when i is a horn or j is a weak homotopy equivalence. The horn case also agrees with the horn pushout-product lifting property in [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. These conclusions include m=0 for boundary inclusions and require no injectivity beyond the given monomorphism j.

source.place: The cartesian Kan--Quillen pushout-product argument for boundary and horn generators; source copy WANTED.

proof.text: By Step 3, r=i\mathbin\square j:D\to Q\times L, with D=(Q\times K)\amalg_{P\times K}(P\times L), is a monomorphism, i.e. a cofibration of the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; hence r has the left lifting property against every trivial Kan fibration (a Kan fibration that is a weak homotopy equivalence). Let p:T\to T' be a trivial fibration of the fixed-object model structure of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus], i.e. a local Kan fibration that is a local weak equivalence; then p(u,v):T(u,v)\to T'(u,v) is a trivial Kan fibration. By the Hom bijection of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction], natural in K (so compatible with precomposition by F^O_{u,v}(r) and r) and in T (so compatible with p and p(u,v)), commutative squares with F^O_{u,v}(r) on the left and p on the right correspond bijectively to commutative squares with r on the left and p(u,v) on the right, and diagonal fillers correspond to diagonal fillers. So F^O_{u,v}(r) has the left lifting property against every trivial fibration of \mathrm{sCat}_O. In a model structure the cofibrations are exactly the maps with the left lifting property against the trivial fibrations, so F^O_{u,v}(r) is a cofibration of \mathrm{sCat}_O, and by Step 2 so is the isomorphic map F^O_{u,v}(i)\mathbin\square j. This holds for every boundary or horn i, every m, and u=v.

proof.text: Suppose i is a horn inclusion or j is a weak homotopy equivalence. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-cartesian-pushout-product] (Step 3), r is then a monomorphism and a weak homotopy equivalence, i.e. a trivial cofibration of the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], so r has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration. A fibration p:T\to T' of the fixed-object model structure of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] is a local Kan fibration, so p(u,v) is a Kan fibration. The same correspondence of squares and fillers as in Step 4, from the natural Hom bijection of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction], shows that F^O_{u,v}(r) has the left lifting property against every fibration of \mathrm{sCat}_O. In a model structure the trivial cofibrations are exactly the maps with the left lifting property against all fibrations, so F^O_{u,v}(r), and by Step 2 the isomorphic map F^O_{u,v}(i)\mathbin\square j, is a trivial cofibration (a cofibration and a local weak equivalence) in exactly these cases; in all cases it is a cofibration by Step 4.

split_report.summary: Audited the fixed-object free-cell statement against the free-arrow adjunction and the Kan--Quillen pushout-product input. Added one genuinely smaller statement-only helper: the simplicial-set cartesian pushout-product lemma. The proof gives the tensor/free-arrow isomorphism, identifies the pushout with the free arrow on the simplicial pushout product, and proves the cofibration and the trivial-cofibration cases by transferring lifting properties along the free-arrow adjunction (maintainer reader's repair: the free-extension argument cited a clause the free-calculus node does not state, and the free-arrow weak-equivalence helper became unnecessary and was dropped).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-15b4ae6f8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement, the parent's six steps and the ancestor's proof paragraph 2. The item's statement is unchanged and true. Checked cases: X empty; u≠v; u=v (free monoid); m=0; j:∅→Δ^0 giving the generator. F is a left adjoint, so it preserves the pushout, and evaluation at (u,v) preserves local (trivial) fibrations, so F is left Quillen. Steps 1–3 are correct. Faults repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-sm7-free-cell.json: (C4) step 4 said the free-calculus node 'declares free extensions to be cofibrations', but that node only says every cofibration is a retract of a free map. Step 4 also said faces carry the new generators to new generators, which is false: for ∂Δ^1→Δ^1 the new edge has old faces. Steps 4 and 5 are rewritten: r is a Kan cofibration, or a trivial cofibration in the horn or weak-j cases (kan-quillen-right-proper plus the new pushout-product helper). Through the natural Hom bijection of the free-arrow adjunction, F(r) then has the left lifting property against trivial fibrations, or against all fibrations, of sCat_O. The free-arrow weak-equivalence helper is then unused; it is true but nothing else cites it, so it is dropped. stmt_deps no longer lists the two helpers, which the statement does not use, and proof_deps is recomputed. The new node lem-coef-kan-quillen-cartesian-pushout-product is kept. It is true (Kan–Quillen is cartesian) and strictly smaller than the item. It does not duplicate sset-anodyne-pushout-product (which lacks the j-weak case and the link between anodyne maps and weak equivalences), the Joyal pushout-product node, or the general SM7 nodes. Its form, searches and blueprint.from/via are correct. Everything stays in sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, with no tool_uses, no cycle and no SGA.
